definitions.explanation: A part of an object designed to be grasped by hand, such as a door handle, pot handle, or drawer pull.

examples.japanese: ドアの{取|と}っ{手|て}を{引|ひ}いた。
この{鍋|なべ}は{取|と}っ{手|て}が{熱|あつ}くならない。
examples.english: The handle of this pot doesn't get hot.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{出|だ}しの{取|と}っ{手|て}が{壊|こわ}れたので{交換|こうかん}した。
examples.english: The drawer handle broke, so I replaced it.

notes:
Written as {取|と}っ{手|て} or {把手|とって}, this refers to any handle designed to be gripped. Very common in everyday life — doors, pots, bags, drawers, and cups all have {取|と}っ{手|て}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドアの{取|と}っ{手|て}: door handle
- {鍋|なべ}の{取|と}っ{手|て}: pot handle
- {取|と}っ{手|て}を{握|にぎ}る: to grip the handle
- {取|と}っ{手|て}を{回|まわ}す: to turn the handle/knob
- {取|と}っ{手|て}{付|つ}き: with a handle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ハンドル: steering wheel; handlebar; also used for door handles in loanword contexts
- {握|にぎ}り: grip (e.g., on a sword or tool)
